To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of RNA extracted from FFPE tissues is dependent on the length of formalin fixation and that the quality of extracted RNA can be improved by amplifying short amplicons.

1. mRNA can be detected in FFPE tissues using real-time RT-PCR, even if the tissues are autolysed or fixed for up to 21 days; 2. the amount of mRNA is reduced in FFPE tissue, but this is more than compensated for by the use of a housekeeping gene for normalization of the data; 3. the amount of RNA extracted from FFPE tissue can be increased by using a short amplicon and a high annealing temperature

the use of sensitive real-time reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction techniques, combined with optimized tissue extraction methods, allows the detection of mRNA in FFPE tissues and that the quality and quantity of mRNA is dependent on tissue autolysis, length of fixation, and the size of the amplicon.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quantitative mRNA analysis in FFPE tissues is feasible, but that the methodological issues are complex, and that further research in this area is required.
quantitative real-time PCR is possible on FFPE tissues, but the method needs to be optimized and standardized for each individual laboratory and application.
quantitative analysis of RNA in FFPE tissues can be done, but that the quality of the results is dependent on the quality of the RNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of real-time PCR and the combination of short amplicons with the use of internal controls, such as beta-actin mRNA, may allow quantitative analysis of mRNA even in archived FFPE tissues.

real-time reverse transcriptases polymerase chain reaction is a powerful tool for the detection of RNA in FFPE tissues and that the quality of RNA can be improved by optimizing the RNA extraction protocol.
quantitative real-time reverse transcription-polymerase reaction analysis of FFPE tissues is possible but that the quality of RNA extracted from FFPE tissues can vary significantly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of mRNA extracted from FFPE tissues is highly dependent on the fixation time, the type of fixation (i.e. buffered versus unbuffered formalin), the length of the amplicon, and the method of extraction.
quantitative mRNA analysis in FFPE tissues is possible, but the results should be expressed relative to a reference gene.
